question: is there a data science minor or certificate at ramapo

The catalog lists a Data Science Minor, and its requirements are CMPS 130 SCI PROBLEM SOLVING-PYTHON, CMPS 240 DATA ANALYTICS IN PYTHON, DATA 101 INTRODUCTION TO DATA SCIENCE, and DATA 301 DATA ANALYSIS & VISUALIZATION; plus select one of BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS, BIOL 354 RESEARCH DESIGN & STATISTICS, MATH 353 STATISTICS, MATH 370 APPLIED STATISTICS, POLI 316 POLITICAL ANALYSIS, PSYC 242 STATISTICS, SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY, or SWRK 307 SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH METHODS. The catalog lists no data science certificate. [15] The catalog describes certificate programs generally, but not a data science certificate. [9][10]

question: how many total credits do u need to graduate from ramapo and how many of those are gen ed
answer:
Undergraduate degrees require at least 128 credits to graduate [5][6][7][10]. The Elementary Education BS requires 128 credits [2]; specific programs may require more [10][15].

For Gen Ed, the published curriculum says students take ten courses: four keystone courses, one in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories [13]. That is a course count, not a credit total; the pages provided do not state a single number of Gen Ed credits. The curriculum should not exceed 41 credits [11].

question: what are the gen ed categories again, i forgot which ones i still need lol
answer:
Ramapo students take four keystone courses—First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities—and one course in each keystone category: Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning. Critical Reading & Writing 102 and Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits. [4]
For distribution, choose one course from two of these three categories: Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics. [4] The Fall 2026 page says the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools. [5]
I can’t tell which categories you personally still need without your Degree Audit. Review it, then make an appointment with your faculty academic advisor about remaining courses. [12] If you believe courses are being applied incorrectly to distribution requirements, email the Registrar at degreeaudit@ramapo.edu. [5]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)

question: whats the recommended order for the comp sci major courses? like what do ppl take sophomore vs junior yr
answer:
The catalog lists the bachelor’s major as Computer Science BS (Bachelor of Science). [13] The recommended plan below applies to students admitted to the major during the 2025–2026 academic year. [1]

- Second Year, Fall Semester (total 16 credits): CMPS 231 - DATA STRUCTURES (4); MATH 237 - DISCRETE STRUCTURES OR MATH 205 - MATHEMATICAL STRUCTURES WI (4); two General Education Requirement * courses (4 credits each); PATH TS2 - CAREER PATHWAYS MODULE 2 FOR THEORETICAL & APPLIED SCIENCE. [1]
- Second Year, Spring Semester (total 16 credits): CMPS 311 - OPERATING SYSTEMS WI (4); CMPS Elective (4); two General Education Requirement * courses (4 credits each); PATH TS3 - CAREER PATHWAYS MODULE 3 FOR THEORETICAL & APPLIED SCIENCE. [1]
- Third Year, Fall Semester (total 16 credits): CMPS 361 - SOFTWARE DESIGN (4); CMPS Elective (4); MATH Elective (4); General Education Requirement * (4). [1]
- Third Year, Spring Semester (total 16 credits): two CMPS Electives (4 credits each); MATH Elective (4); General Education Requirement * (4). [1]

The plan is 128 credits total. [1] It also lists Computer Science with MS in Applied Mathematics 4+1, Computer Science with MS in Computer Science 4+1, and Computer Science with MS in Data Science 4+1 as other plans for that year. [1] Plan: https://www.ramapo.edu/recommended-graduation-plan-2025/tas/computer-science/

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-CMPS) [13](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: comm major reqs + is there a capstone or internship requirement
answer:
The catalog lists two bachelor’s majors for “comm”: Communication Arts BA and Visual Communication Design BA [14]. Requirements differ, so “comm major” doesn’t identify one specific set.

Communication Arts BA (Bachelor of Arts): The catalog has Digital Journalism and Writing and Global Communication and Media concentrations. Both require a capstone portfolio course and CNTP 388 CO-OP/INTERNSHIP CONTEMPORARY ARTS [1]. Course requirements depend on concentration; see the [Communication Arts catalog requirements](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-COMM).

Visual Communication Design BA (Bachelor of Arts): Requires the listed major courses, one history/theory/criticism course, one 200- or 300-level history/theory/criticism course (any 200- or 300-level Art History (ARHT) course can also fulfill this), one visual communication elective, and one capstone course. It also requires CNTP 388 CO-OP/INTERNSHIP CONTEMPORARY ARTS. Concentrations have additional required courses; the Game Design and Immersive Media concentration notes to consult a faculty advisor for 2 additional course requirements [2]. See the [Visual Communication Design catalog requirements](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-VSCD).

Both majors therefore list a capstone and an internship requirement [1][2].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-COMM) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-VSCD) [14](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: should i switch to psych or just add it as a minor? i dont want to graduate late
answer:

A minor must include 16–24 credits (including non-General Education prerequisites and excluding lab science course credits); major courses may overlap, but no more than half the minor credits may overlap [11]. An undergraduate degree includes General Education, a major, and free electives; a minor and/or second major are options [14].

I can’t verify which choice would let you graduate on time for your individual record, or recommend one without your remaining requirements. Check your Graduation Plan and meet with Academic Advising to map your remaining courses; the college says most majors require at least two years, and advises using Graduation Plans to assess whether you can add a minor [2, 5]. The Registrar says major changes are recommended before the next registration cycle [9].

If you decide to make a change, the Registrar’s page says review requirements, email the convener to schedule a meeting, then submit the online form; don’t submit multiple requests [7]. Another Registrar page says complete the online form and recommends changes before the next registration cycle [9]. question: whats the difference between the marketing concentration in bus admin and the marketing minor
